title: Heroes Analysis: Values You Aspire To
opening: When someone inspires you, what did that person do? Look at the action and what you know about it.
actions: Identify people whose actions inspire you.
Name the particular qualities and the examples that support them.
Compare recurring qualities and narrow to the strongest examples.
Name the candidate values and examine an appropriate expression in your own life.

teaching.use: Use this when inspiration is present but its underlying value is unclear.
teaching.distinction: A person can show one quality without serving as a model for every part of life.
teaching.evidence: Use specific actions or work as evidence. Mark your interpretation as an interpretation.
teaching.guardrail: Fame, wealth, or success does not prove virtue. Do not copy a whole life from one admired quality.
teaching.independentSource: You can find values through direct experience without using a hero. This exercise is one source, not a required identity task.
teaching.tryIt: Choose one admired act and remove the person's name. Would the act still matter if an unknown person performed it?

labels.reflectionPrompt: Write about the people or acts you choose, the qualities you see, and the examples behind your view. You can start with one act. Add, change, or remove any part. A candidate value or a possible expression in your own life can remain uncertain.

feedback.unavailable: Private notes cannot be saved here. Your note remains on screen.
feedback.missing: Write a note before saving. You can leave parts of the reflection open.
feedback.length: Shorten the note to 2,000 characters or fewer.
feedback.readFailure: The saved note could not be loaded. Your current note remains here.
feedback.conflict: This note changed elsewhere. Your answer remains here; compare before saving again.
feedback.readbackFailure: The save could not be confirmed. Retry to check the same save.
feedback.saveFailure: The save is uncertain. Retry the same note.
feedback.retryPending: The earlier save is unresolved. Retry the same note before changing it.
